description: methodology 1.8 / 3.5 — the learning rates. Production trains the shared network at 3e-4 and the free per-user fields at 1e-2, a ratio of about 33x; the arms named `shipped` are that configuration. The questions: whether one shared rate diverges late and in evaluation mode (it does not) and what it costs on held-out problems against the split (nothing — slightly better at every seed); whether a 10x ratio differs from 33x (unresolved); and whether a three-times-slower network at the 1e-2 field rate reaches the same fit (slightly worse at every seed, same plateau epoch). THE PANEL DOES NOT DECIDE THE SPLIT: its arms hold whole problems aside and are not calibrated, and on the production configuration's calibrated held-row loss, same rows and paired by initialisation, the shared rate is 1 mnat worse with the slope barrier (one seed) and, without it, 7 mnat worse at one seed and 1.7 better at another, so the panel's unanimous sign is absent on the loss that ships and the split stays. EVERY ARM RUNS AT THREE SEEDS. Within one seed all arms hold aside the SAME stop rows, so each cross-arm held-out delta is paired; the further seeds are independent repeats of that paired delta, there because the reference configuration's own trace wanders wider than the contrasts asked about, so one arm per configuration resolves none of them.
